caption: Rescaled microplastic concentrations in Dutch rivers and the four Monterey Bay rivers, (a) rescaled to 50–500 µm (W2, primary: interior to every measured range) and (b) extrapolated to 1–5000 µm (W1). Open symbols, per-sample median; thin bars, per-sample 5–95% Monte Carlo interval; thick point ranges, median and interquartile range of the per-sample medians for each water body; symbol shape, analytical technique; colour, dataset. Row labels give the differential slope a used to rescale that row and the number of samples; this study's W2 rows are measurements, so the river-specific fitted slope is shown there for reference. Value types: Dutch W2 and W1, reconstructed here with the RIVM uncertainty method (triangular α and ±10% size limits); “+”, RIVM's own published per-sample medians (W1 only); this study W2, measured (50–500 µm sieve fraction, CF = 1); this study W1, reconstructed from each river's own single slope. Dutch FTIR slopes were fitted above xmin ≈ 170–270 µm but are applied down to 20 µm; W1 differences are dominated by slope and should be read as secondary. Dommel combines Mintenig et al. (2020) and Mintenig et al. (2025). Slope convention: differential PSD slope a (dN/dL ∝ L^a); RIVM's positive PDF exponent α is converted as a = −α. Fitting methods differ: Dutch slopes are poweRlaw maximum-likelihood fits above an estimated xmin to particles ≤ 5000 µm, aggregated per water body and technique (Quik et al. 2026); this study's slopes are C-PSD fits within the Segur et al. (2026) LOD window. Systems differ: large perennial Dutch rivers and a canal (FTIR, Mintenig et al. 2020, 2025; LDIR, Mughini-Gras et al. 2021) versus discrete pumped samples from small, episodic Central Coast rivers (µFTIR). Dutch concentrations are study-reported totals (authors' blank and subsampling corrections), not recomputed from particles.
